column1: # INTERACTIONS -- who was in the room, and what happened. Append-only.
# *** THIS IS THE FILE THE CAMPAIGN HAS BEEN MISSING. ***
# Social events lived ONLY in prose -- three thousand lines of it -- which is
# why "narrating from my own summary instead of from the log" is the largest
# error class in this campaign. Every one of these was a query that could not be
# run:
#   how Kell died          ..  narrated backwards
#   Sim's two years        ..  wrong
#   Cuddy toward Yrtone    ..  called cold; npcs.md said the opposite
#   Ista's grievance       ..  extended to a cart trip it never covered
#   the barrel "never moved" .. world_changes.tsv:419 says otherwise
#   "the plan was the 51st" .. the DM's own calendar row, read back as theirs
#   Meg and Tibb           ..  a mother and her grown son, written as two families
#   "you nearly forgot Wend" .. they had been the ones reminding him
# `people` is a COMMA LIST on purpose: it has to be typeable at the table. The
# build normalises it into a proper join, and the validator REFUSES any name
# that does not resolve to campaign/people.tsv -- so "Wetherby", "Rell's
# brother" and a typo are all caught at the moment of writing.
# `seq` numbers the scenes within a day, so `evidence` elsewhere can point at
# "77:3" and mean something exact.
# `kind`: first_contact | counsel | negotiation | promise | payment | grievance
#         | teaching | report | conflict | fact
#   `fact` is for a dated thing that is true of somebody and will stop being
#   true -- "Cuddy is frail" -- which is an EVENT, not a property, and filing it
#   as a property is how Ancel's "Unanswered" outlived its answer by 43 days.
# `reaction` is the d100 where one was rolled. MOST OF THE TIME THERE IS NONE:
# DMG p.63 is a FIRST-CONTACT mechanic and rolling it at friends was itself one
# of the errors (four times in one hour). Blank means no roll, deliberately.
# SEEDED 2026-09-11 from campaign/sessions/. Not every scene -- the ones a query
# would be run against: first contacts, the reactions, the promises, and the
# findings. `evidence` points at the session file, which is verbatim and
# complete.
day
column8: summary
THE SURETY. Dave answerable for Hask, Dellie, Corm and Sarn by name and aloud. Nothing on paper either way; the condition is that the four must be visibly WORKING
Met on the road, half-day 1 of the patrol. Neutral until Dave named Ottir. Had driven the whole lonely stretch and seen nothing, and TOLD THE MARKET SO UNPROMPTED, naming the party
NOT DOWN THE HOLE -- I'll not ask that of anybody who isn't paid to take that kind of risk. Dave will not ask any hired man into the caves. A promise, not a preference
WEND COMES ROUND BEFORE ANYONE SPOKE -- not for the money and not for the argument, but because they walked the road publicly for six days. "I got it from watching"
Coll's standing instruction: bring in anyone desperate and put them to work. "If people need work I trust your judgement." He did exactly that and wrote down what each was owed
Marrow asked DAVE to ask his son what he wanted, because he could not. "I suppose I thought if he said he wanted to stay, I'd have to let him"

Reaction 11, BADLY FRIGHTENED -- pulled to 81 when Dave took his mail off in the road where the crossbowman could watch. Came north TO BUY, on a rumour. Asked Osk who to speak to about next summer's wool
WEND TAKES THE FACTORSHIP. Her price is the succession document: two years, then she spends it on the town as she sees fit
Dave quoted Sim to his father word for word. Marrow asked the boy directly for the first time in two years and got his "Aye." THE THREAD CLOSES

*** THE ANSWER TO ANCEL'S QUESTION, TWO DAYS AFTER HE ASKED IT. *** He cannot buy the clip and says so, then names FOUR BUYERS who do not know Wethersby exists -- two raw-wool men east of Marchford, a FULLER WHO TAKES CLOTH, and a factor's man. A penny in the pound for three years; he asked two and Wend haggled him up
Brokered by Wend. Marrow made him say the four names twice, then where they were and what they bought. Marrow bought him his dinner
GYLL PAYS RESTITUTION TO THE ELEVEN, 4 gp 10 sp apiece, selling the grey mare to cover the shortfall, SAID ALOUD IN THE SQUARE with Ottir witnessing
The leg mends clean and he will not limp. HE CANNOT READ AND HE ASKED TO LEARN
The buyer of last resort agreed -- 8 gp the tod, cap 500 the season. She needs a CLERK and DOES NOT KNOW SARN HAS BEEN KEEPING THE TALLY
THE SURETY IS SATISFIED. Wace has written: the account of the hundred at Draycot on day 52. Ottir asked the one hard question about Quasqueton -- whose is it?
*** HALM'S STANDING WANT, asked once and never again: "One load's a load. What I'd want, someday, is a RUN. Osk's got a run. He knows where he is on a Tuesday." ***
Met riding north. Usher of the hall, buying a bed for a spring wedding. Gave away WHY WACE WROTE, for nothing, and it defused everything
The chest gets read. He has the run of it, nobody minds an almoner reading, and ten days
THE SKELETONS TOLD AND HOLY WATER REFUSED. Cuddy is a cleric of the 3rd; DMG p.114 requires the 5th, and his chapel has no font
THE DWARF IN IRONS, told second and should have been first. "I have never once had to be told about a man forty years late." His one flat instruction: BRING HIM OUT

THE CRAG. The title cannot be settled from that chest -- but a grant NAMING ROGAHN AND ZELLIGAR, to hold of the lord FOR THE KEEPING OF THE NORTH WAY. Counsel: do not raise the title, ask for the LICENCE
THE PETITION. The licence GRANTED AS ASKED and backdated to Michaelmas last. He never read the perambulation -- d6=4, vindicating Cuddy completely
SHE FINDS THE HOLE NOBODY ELSE SAW: the licence says stone and timber, and it is not a bill of sale for a dead wizard's balances
THE DOUBLE BIND, CALLED OUT AND DISSOLVED. "Let me spend it" read as asking permission that was not the party's to give. The rule that came out of it is about POWER, NOT PHRASING
THE MESSAGE TO ISTA WENT BADLY
He finds the SAME hole four hours later -- corroboration, not coincidence. AND HE FINDS THE TRICK: ask for nothing substantive, then ask for A RECEIPT, because a receipt recites what the letter said

Why's the glass smoked? Somebody paid extra so this could sit in the dark. THE VIAL IS REALGAR -- a pigment, poisonous, degrades in light. He opened it himself in shade with a wet rag, everyone else eight feet back
The realgar sold for 35 gp

THE DYE AT COST, AND THE FIRST FINDING RUNS AGAINST THE PARTY. At cost is a discount and a discount is a gift wearing a trade's clothes -- and then Dave put a FIGURE on it and it went to 5. "Thirty years telling people what's in a jar for nothing and nobody's ever costed it"
HASK SELLS THE SMALL GOODS AND DOES NOT UNDERSELL, holding his number through two silences. 160 gp. THE LINE CLOSES: 573 on 357
FATHER DOULE IS FIFTH LEVEL -- Cuddy's lead was good -- AND MARCHFORD HAS NO FONT. "I can make it. I have never made it." The priest and the vessel are in different towns
Dill is the missing link in the party's own cloth chain, and he is a DRESSER, not a labourer
He holds to his terms exactly. 31 gp at his door; 18 owing in three quarterly instalments

ELEVEN SHILLINGS LENT TO DILL for his tools -- and he asked for it to be written as a DEBT, repayable out of his first month, rather than taken as a gift. articles.md's first finding running the right way round: a job cancels a debt, a gift deepens one, and he chose the form himself
PAID ~250 GP, his full valuation, the moment he was shown Wace's receipt. His day-42 condition DISCHARGED after twenty-three days. Over a thousand gold for the first time
THE LOOM IS NARROW -- and she turns it round: "It isn't one weaver too many. IT'S ONE LOOM TOO FEW." She REFUSES THE CARTS as a gift and proposes letting them at the wear
HOLT NAMES THE CASK OFF THE BUNG without tapping it -- strong stock ale, thirty years and not turned. 58 gp: 30 in coin and 28 in his own hand, written unasked
THE STRUCTURE SIGNED, articles.md art. 13. 300 gp wage reserve, cash, locked, NO exception clause. Fair copy in SARN'S hand, witnessed by OTTIR

*** NAN CAN GRADE WOOL. *** Nine years on Rell's ground, and she knows WHOSE -- Ellery honest, two past Wettleford roll theirs wet, Marrow's the best in the hundred, and a widow at Hobb's Lane with three years of it in a loft. "Nobody has ever asked her a single question about wool. Including me"
CUDDY IS FRAIL. The wet in his chest, seventy-odd, November. Not dying, and it did not show in September

*** A MAN HAS BEEN SENT ABOUT THE ANIMATED DEAD. *** His house did not write to ask questions -- it wrote to say a man is coming. "In thirty years I have never once had a letter that said somebody was coming"
He asks Dellie to learn the words for the dwarf -- "not today, in case" -- and teaches her for an hour at the table. "There ought to be two of us who can and not one"

THE ROOF. He does not know and will not guess -- and reframes it: "Whose is it is the wrong end of it. They ask WHO MENDED IT LAST, and who paid the man." PERRIN STRUCK OFF because he refers upward. He will not carry it himself
NO AMOUNTS, and she owns it: "You asked me for a list and I gave you a list. A LIST ISN'T AN ORDER." It does not fit one cart. The loom goes to BERN. One addition: flax seed
The Draycot almonry account: 10 gp a year on Wend's books IN HIS NAME, a sum he DRAWS and renders. Not a purse across a table

*** THE CARRIAGE GAP. *** She had already found it and had not raised it. Carriage follows WEIGHT: the iron was 14% of the Ludbury load's value and 51% of its weight, so "at cost" was 50-70 gp BELOW cost. On Osk she has NO VIEW AT ALL and says so, naming Halm and the trap in the same breath: ask what is DONE

THE TWO CLOCKS, ruled 2026-09-11 on the player's question. Gyll's "I've had two year to find something else to say" is NOT a slip: his eleven were turned off TWO YEARS AGO when the wool staple moved and Rell died, while the road only went bad weeks before day 1. district.md already said it -- "the robberies are DOWNSTREAM... all the same event, MONTHS APART." Hask has robbed roads for twenty-two years and had never worked THIS one until a week before the party met him, so he was never one of Rell's eleven
